claim: data/instruments.md:41 "23 (five factors), **settled at search-summary level** ... The earlier \"22 items\" came from one secondary description and is not supported ... Study 3 fit reported as mixed (robust CFI 0.91, robust RMSEA 0.13, search-summary level)" and data/instruments.md:64 "OMS-WA (23 items, search-summary level; 11 or 9 if a short form is chosen)"
evidence: VERIFIER R2 2026-10-09, WebSearch, search-summary level only (link.springer.com, d-nb.info and sciencedirect are unreachable from here). (1) 23 is supported only as the Study 1 EFA result (five factors, 23 items, N = 207, from a 27-item pool; one passage gives N = 209). Two extended searches confirmed this. (2) '22 is not supported' is contradicted. An extended search on Szeto, Dobson & Knaak 2019, the Road to Mental Readiness meta-analysis (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6591743/), relays its methods: the OMS-WA is a 22-item scale with five subscales (avoidance; dangerousness/unpredictability; workplace attitudes; helping; responsibility), scored 1 to 5. A second summary says the 11-item short-form paper (doi 10.1037/cbs0000350) notes that earlier studies used 22 items with five subscales. A third says the 2024 paper's first-responder CFA used 22 items. Study 3's samples (N = 5385 and 1207, confirmed by search) are baseline data from the same national programmes. So the version actually administered at scale may well be 22 items, and the count is unresolved between 22 and 23, not 'settled'. (3) The Study 3 fit figures (robust CFI 0.91, RMSEA 0.13) did not appear in two extended searches. The summaries relay the abstract as 'good model fit' with both samples, and an RMSEA of 0.13 would usually be read as poor fit. Label them unverified or remove them. Fix: at :41 and :64 say '22 or 23, unresolved (23 = Study 1 EFA; 22 = the five-subscale version used in the R2MR / Working Mind evaluations, search-summary level)', drop 'settled' and 'not supported', and mark the CFI/RMSEA unverified.
